subject: Sprint-zero kickoff: indexing backfill priorities & vector DB tradeoffs
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@heliosmedia.com>, Kyle Morgan <kyle.morgan@heliosmedia.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-26T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Sprint-zero kickoff: indexing backfill priorities & vector DB tradeoffs

Hi Ana / Kyle —

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Per our conversation, I’ve pulled together a short Sprint‑Zero agenda to align scope and acceptance criteria for the embeddings -> rerank migration. Goal is to lock the next 4 weeks of work so your engineering and cloudops teams can schedule the maintenance window for the index backfill.

High level asks from Helios:
- Prioritize search relevance parity for the homepage and top 10 article pages
- Keep peak query latency under 120ms P50 for search endpoint during hard-cutover
- Minimal downtime for editorial indexing (target < 15 minutes for cutover)

Proposed Sprint‑Zero items (attachments included):
1) Data readiness checklist and sampling (rerank_eval_prompts.csv) — Marissa will run a 5k sample to sanity check embeddings/relevance.
2) Vector DB decision & config — HNSW memory footprint vs IVF+PQ cost tradeoffs; we recommend HNSW with dynamic M tuning for initial pilot.
3) Index backfill plan (index_backfill_estimates.xlsx) — parallel shards, throttling plan, and estimated run time for 24M docs.
4) Acceptance tests — automated rerank smoke tests, precision@3 for top queries, and live A/B baseline comparison.
5) Ops runbook and rollback — short rollback plan if latency/regressions exceed thresholds.

Can Monica and Marissa confirm owners for 1–4? Also tagging Vivek for a quick comment on quantization/embedding size tradeoffs (8-bit vs 16-bit) and cost implications.

I’ve attached a 1‑page sprint0_agenda.pdf and the backfill estimate workbook. If this looks good I’ll propose a 60‑minute kickoff for Monday 10am PT where we review the sample outputs and finalize the maintenance window.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

--- attachments: sprint0_agenda.pdf (pdf), index_backfill_estimates.xlsx (xlsx), rerank_eval_prompts.csv (csv) ---

Subject: Re: Sprint-zero kickoff: indexing backfill priorities & vector DB tradeoffs

Jordan —

Thanks, this looks aligned with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Our editorial team can tolerate a 30‑minute article search inconsistency window during the cutover if that helps sequencing.
- Cloudops prefers an IVF+PQ pilot for the first run because we can hot‑swap nodes more easily; they’re open to HNSW if we can validate memory and restart time in staging.

Owners: I’ll own scheduling with Cloudops and provide VM specs; Kyle will coordinate editorial sampling for the rerank eval prompts.

Monday 10am PT works for us — please send a calendar invite.

Best,
Ana Ruiz
Head of Product, Helios Media
ana.ruiz@heliosmedia.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-26T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint-zero kickoff: indexing backfill priorities & vector DB tradeoffs

Jordan / team —

I’ll take owner for the acceptance tests and the cutover smoke plan. Proposed checkpoints:
- Week 0 (this week): Marissa produces 5k sample embeddings + basic rerank precision report.
- Week 1: Staging backfill (5% sample of production corpus) — verify throughput and restart time.
- Week 2: Full backfill dry run during low traffic window (overnight) — measure wall clock and peak mem.
- Week 3: Production cutover and 48h monitoring window.

Acceptance thresholds I propose: precision@3 >= baseline - 2%, P50 latency < 120ms, error rate < 0.5%. If any are missed we trigger roll‑forward to fallback model variant.

Also adding an item: we should capture the embedding vector size matrix (dim, dtype, quantization) in the workbook so Cloudops has exact storage forecasts. I’ll update index_backfill_estimates.xlsx and reattach.

— Monica
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-26T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint-zero kickoff: indexing backfill priorities & vector DB tradeoffs

Quick technical notes from my end:
- I ran an initial 5k sample overnight using our default 1536-d float16 embeddings. Results: recall@10 holds ~98% vs baseline for the sampled queries; rerank precision@3 is slightly lower (~95% of baseline) on tail queries. CSV attached (rerank_eval_prompts.csv).
- For vector DBs: HNSW with M=16 and efConstruction=200 gave the best recall in staging but memory per shard is ~1.2GB per 1M vectors at 1536-d fp16. IVF+PQ reduces memory by ~60% but increased P50 by ~30ms.
- Recommendation: Start with IVF+PQ for the first backfill to reduce memory impact and run an HNSW pilot on a single shard to validate latency at scale.

I’ll be ready Monday to walk through the sample outputs and show the rerank test harness. Vivek — can you confirm if we should try 8-bit quantization for the production embedding storage? Thinking about perf vs model-quality regression risk.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

--- attachment: rerank_eval_prompts.csv (csv) ---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-26T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint-zero kickoff: indexing backfill priorities & vector DB tradeoffs

Folks —

Short answer: yes, test 8‑bit asymmetric quantization on the staging sample but gate it behind the evaluation harness. My notes:
- 8-bit reduces storage ~2x and improves cache behavior on CPUs; quality drop usually minimal for 1536-d on natural-language corpora but varies by prompt.
- For rerank, we should include a small high‑sensitivity eval set (500 queries with editorial labels) so we can catch regressions in tail cases.
- If we use IVF+PQ, ensure we store a small dense residual for top candidates to improve final re‑scoring.

I’ll prepare a short script to produce quantized vectors and a delta report vs fp16 for Monday.

— Vivek
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

One ask from editorial: can you include a short checklist for how to validate non‑search surfaces (recommendations, related articles) that might be affected by embedding changes? We want to avoid regressions outside of main search.

See you Monday.

Best,
Ana
